identity.name: Perpetual Calendar Split-Seconds Chronograph
identity.one_liner: The 5004 is the perpetual calendar split-seconds chronograph that defined the modern Patek grand complication — produced 1995-2012, the last hand-wound perpetual chrono before the 5204 took over.

narrative.story: The 5004 is a Lemania base caliber (Lemania 2320) modified by Patek, with a perpetual calendar, split-seconds, and a leap-year indicator. The split-seconds (rattrapante) lets the wearer time two events that start together but end at different times — useful for race timing, photography, and stopping a chronograph without losing the original reading. The 5004G (white gold, 1995) and 5004J (yellow gold, 1996) and 5004R (rose gold) and 5004P (platinum) are all four produced 1995-2012, with the platinum at 250 examples. The 5004 is the most-cited split-seconds perpetual of the 1990s-2010s.
narrative.collector_notes: The 5004P is the grail: 250 examples, and the only platinum Patek with both a perpetual and a split-seconds. Look for the Breguet numerals, the small seconds at 9, the 30-minute counter at 3, the day/date sub-dials at 6.
